setup.why: route is workspace/admin scoped (/api/v1/admin-v2/settings/templates), not project-scoped — no project or fixture object needed

notes:
First attempt succeeded (no failed attempts, no setup calls needed). Response returned the two known system templates for this workspace: id 1164 'Test Case Steps' (is_default:true, is_system:true, step_type:test_case_steps) and id 1664 'Test Case BDD' (is_default:false, is_system:true, step_type:test_case_bdd) — matches the confirmed fixture pool exactly. `info` was correctly absent since `paginated` was not sent (contract says info only appears when paginated=true); this is documented conditional behaviour, not a missing field, so not counted as declared_missing. All declared response keys (success, templates[].{id,name,entity,enabled,step_type,is_default,is_system,future_projects_applicable,field_count,linked_to_all_projects,project_count,created_at,updated_at}) were present and populated (field_count/linked_to_all_projects/project_count came back null, which the contract documents as a valid 'not computed' state, not absence).

SPECIFIC INTEREST — list_test_case_templates_v2 vs list_templates_v2: the two are NOT interchangeable and the difference is real, not cosmetic. (1) entity_type: list_test_case_templates_v2 takes a REQUIRED `entity_type` query param (values TestCase | TestRunResult) — omitting it errors rather than defaulting, per its own guidance ('entity_type is effectively REQUIRED even though it reads as optional... always send it'). list_templates_v2 has NO entity_type param at all — the entity is fixed server-side to TestCase only, so it can never list TestRunResult templates. This confirms the routing-eval report: entity_type is exactly what separates them, and only one of the two accepts it. (2) Scope/route: list_test_case_templates_v2 hits the workspace/admin-scoped /api/v1/admin-v2/settings/templates route (no project param binds results to a project, though an optional `project` filter narrows by linkage); list_templates_v2's describeCapability output does not show this admin path and instead documents ordinary p/count paging. (3) Pagination mechanics differ: list_test_case_templates_v2 pages only when `paginated` is literally the string 'true' (fixed page size 10, `p` otherwise ignored); list_templates_v2 pages via `p` + `count` (page size up to 300, `page`/`per_page` are explicitly ignored aliases). (4) Neither capability's contract carries a preferred or deprecated marker in describeCapability's output — no `deprecated`, `preferred`, or superseded-by field appears on either. So beyond entity_type/pagination-shape, nothing in the contracts states one should be chosen over the other; that omission is itself worth flagging to whoever owns capability selection guidance, since two overlapping list-templates capabilities with no preference signal is exactly what causes routing-eval confusion.

CONTRACT DEFECT — the declared 200 schema for list_test_case_templates_v2 is still the empty literal `{"type":"object"}` (see the raw describeCapability output: `"responses":{"200":{"description":"...","schema":{"type":"object"}}}`). The prose `description` string does list the real shape (success, templates[] with the field list), but the machine-checkable `schema` itself declares nothing — no `properties`, no `required`, not even `type: array` on `templates`. This is a live defect independent of what the API actually returned: a 2xx contract that type-checks against literally any object payload cannot be used to validate a response programmatically, and it means the `returns` field of the top-level contract (which does list the real keys) and the nested `responses.200.schema` disagree with each other in the same describeCapability payload. By contrast, list_templates_v2's schema is fully typed (required/properties down to per-field types on templates[] items and info{}), so this is specific to list_test_case_templates_v2, not a systemic issue across both capabilities.
